sentence: This project studies how a protective pathway in the liver controls bile acid metabolism in liver diseases.
This project tests gene-editing drugs delivered in exosomes to see whether they can clear chronic viral infection and avoid off-target effects.
This project studies the molecular, genetic and developmental reasons that multiple traits become linked and appear together as one complex phenotype.
This project studies how a non-canonical Rho GTPase protein is controlled in lung cancer and how it affects metastasis.
This project tests whether treating alcohol-associated hepatitis and alcohol use disorder together helps patients with severe alcohol-associated hepatitis.
This project studies how dopamine function and the brain relate to depression as it develops from adolescence into young adulthood.
This project builds a platform that takes 3D images of engineered tissue without damaging it, using photoacoustic microscopy.
This project tries to understand the structures that form the internal skeleton of apicomplexan parasites that cause serious human diseases.
This project measures the biomechanical properties of the aorta in mouse models of thoracic aortopathy and links them to gene activity using deep learning.
This project examines long-term outcomes for patients after peripheral vascular interventions for peripheral arterial disease, using linked registry and electronic health records.
This project explores a combination therapy that targets signaling pathways in transformed cells.
This project develops inhibitors of a methyltransferase from the virus that causes COVID-19 and aims for broad-spectrum antivirals.
This project tests whether blocking a serotonin receptor makes uveal melanoma cells more sensitive to inhibitors of a mutant signaling pathway.
This project focuses on heart health and disease, especially heart failure.
This project uses protein footprinting with mass spectrometry to study how amyloid beta protein clumps together in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how antimicrobial resistance develops and spreads in aquaculture bacteria and builds tools to detect it earlier.
This project studies how ion channels control the inner machinery of immune cells that protect against infections and keep tissues healthy.
This project re-engineers CRISPR-associated transposons, which insert DNA at chosen sites without double-strand breaks, to work better in many organisms.
This project describes immune-related genes and their alleles in nonhuman primates and builds genotyping technologies to read them.
This project studies how the mitochondrion makes, stores and converts energy within the cell.
